paper_title: First Axion-Like Particle Results from a Broadband Search for Wave-Like Dark Matter in the 44 to 52 $μ$eV Range with a Coaxial Dish Antenna
coupling_convention: |g_agamma| in GeV^-1, as plotted on linear y-axis with x10^-11 multiplier
notes: First ALP (axion-photon) search with a dish antenna (BREAD coaxial reflector in a 3.9 T solenoid at Argonne), covering 44-52 ueV (10.7-12.5 GHz). Coupling type is unambiguous (g_agamma, Eq. 1-2), DM density assumption 0.45 GeV/cm^3 from Eq. 2, 90% CL stated. However, the paper provides NO numerical limit values in text or tables; the exclusion is shown only in Fig. 3 (not machine-readable here). The paper states it is the most stringent laboratory constraint in this range, i.e. below the CAST bound of ~6.6e-11 GeV^-1. The emitted two-point flat line at ~5e-11 GeV^-1 across the stated 44-52 ueV validity range is an ESTIMATE consistent with that claim; actual limit varies with frequency and should be replaced with digitized Fig. 3 data (e.g. from AxionLimits repository) for precision. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.75, 56)) | Vision: Fig 3(a) shows the GigaBREAD 90% CL exclusion (green region) on |g_agamma| for ALPs in 44.3-51.7 ueV (10.7-12.5 GHz). Linear-linear axes; y-axis multiplier x10^-11 GeV^-1 applied. The boundary is highly jagged (fluctuating between ~3.4e-11 and ~4.7e-11 GeV^-1 with narrow masked-bin spikes reaching the CAST region at ~5.7e-11); points trace the typical envelope of the limit curve rather than every narrow spike. Surrounding constraints shown: CAST (~5.7e-11), SN1987A, Globular clusters, NuSTAR. rho_0 = 0.45 GeV/cm^3 assumed. Coupling type unambiguous: ALP-photon coupling from dish antenna in 3.9 T field. | Calibration: No calibration needed (benchmark KSVZ raw_ratio=1.02 snapped to identity)
